input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having a bit of trouble with my phone. It’s been saying “No Service” for the past few hours, and I’m not sure what to do. Can you help me get it working again?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Do you need anything else from me?
Oh, I see. Yes, please go ahead and send me the payment request. I’d like to get this sorted out so my phone works again.
I’ve just completed the payment for the overdue bill. What should I do next to get my phone working again?
Oh, I get a bit nervous about restarting my phone—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do this? Could you please reassure me before I go ahead?
Alright, I’ve restarted my phone like you said, but it still shows “No Signal” at the top. Is there something else I should try?

I’m not sure about the make and model, to be honest—it’s just a basic smartphone, nothing fancy. Could you guide me through what to check? I get confused with all the settings, so step-by-step help would be great.
At the top of my screen, it still shows “No Signal” and “Data Disabled.” The battery is at 80%. There aren’t any other icons showing. What should I do next?
It looks like Airplane Mode is OFF, but I also see something about the SIM card status saying “missing.” Does that mean my SIM card isn’t working? What should I do now?

Alright, I’ve followed your instructions and reinserted the SIM card, then turned my phone back on. Unfortunately, it still says “No Signal” at the top. Is there anything else I can try? This is getting a bit frustrating.
It says my SIM card is active and working. But I still don’t have any signal showing. What should I do next?
It says the network mode preference is set to “4G/5G preferred.” Does that sound right, or should I change it to something else?
It says that mobile data is enabled, and the SIM card is active. But it still shows “No Signal” and no cellular connection. Is there anything else I can try?
It says the current APN name is “broken,” and there’s something about an MMSC URL for picture messages. I’m not sure what any of that means—should I change something here?

I’ve reset the APN settings and restarted my phone. Now, at the top of the screen, it shows full signal bars, 5G, and data is enabled! It looks like everything is working again. Thank you so much for your help!
Thank you, I really appreciate your patience and guidance. I’ll reach out if I need help again. Have a wonderful day! ###STOP###

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.
